title: Looker Query Queue and Concurrency Saturation
dataSources: Looker System Activity Explores (`looker:system_activity`), Looker API (`looker:api`), and instance logs.
app: Looker System Activity (i__looker) via DB Connect or the Looker API (`/api/4.0`); Looker instance logs via Universal Forwarder; scheduled plan and query events via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=looker:system_activity source="history"
| bin _time span=5m
| stats avg(runtime) as avg_runtime, sum(eval(status="error")) as errors, count as queries by _time
| eventstats avg(queries) as baseline
| where queries>baseline*1.5
| sort - _time
description: Watches Looker query throughput from the System Activity history Explore and flags windows where concurrent query volume spikes beyond baseline, driving queue waits and connection-pool contention.
value: Concurrency spikes make every Looker dashboard slow at once; catching them lets teams add query slots or tune connections before users complain.
implementation: Query the System Activity history Explore via API or DB Connect; schedule every 5 minutes and alert on sustained above-baseline concurrency.
visualization: Timechart of queries and runtime, saturation markers.
grandmaExplanation: We watch how many reports Looker is running at once so we can add capacity before everything slows down together.
